sentence_stem: If the company had listened to its employees years ago,
correct_completion: it would be much more successful today.
full_sentence: If the company had listened to its employees years ago, it would be much more successful today.
acceptable_variants: it would be a leader in its field.
it would not be struggling now.

options.text: it has been successful for years.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect states a fact. A mixed conditional needs a hypothetical present result, so this does not complete the sentence.

options.text: it would be much more successful today.
so it did not change its policy.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals cause and effect, but the sentence needs a hypothetical result of the unreal past condition.

options.text: it will succeed if it listens today.
options.why_wrong: A first conditional about the future does not complete the unreal past condition set up by 'had listened'.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result
explanation: A mixed conditional combines a past condition (had plus past participle) with a present result (would plus base verb). Spanish speakers may keep one tense throughout, but English requires the past perfect in the if-clause and would plus the base form in the result.
translation: Si la empresa hubiera escuchado a sus empleados hace años, hoy sería mucho más exitosa.
